level.title: Korean B1+ — CV and interview
goals: Describe your experience and duties in the past tense the CV uses
Answer interview questions with a result, not an adjective
Discuss salary, start date and conditions without closing the door

lessons.title: 경력을 정리해요
lessons.learn: A CV lists what you did, for how long and with what result: 삼 년 동안 고객 지원을 담당했고, 응답 시간을 절반으로 줄였습니다.

grammar.title: Stating experience
grammar.pattern: 삼 년 동안 담당했습니다 · 응답 시간을 줄였습니다 · 기간은 이 년입니다
grammar.explain: A duty is 담당하다 and a result takes a number and a change verb: 줄이다, 늘리다, 개선하다. Duration takes 동안, and the past tense of a CV stays in 합니다체.

examples.t: 삼 년 동안 고객 지원을 담당했습니다.
examples.r: sam nyeon dongan gogaek jiwon-eul damdanghaetseumnida.
examples.en: I was in charge of customer support for three years.
I cut the response time by half.
The project ran for two years.

mistakes.why: A duration takes 동안, not 을/를.
줄이다 is transitive: the time is the object.

dialogue.en: When were you in charge of this work?

dialogue.t: 이 년 전부터 삼 년 동안 담당했습니다.
dialogue.r: i nyeon jeon-buteo sam nyeon dongan damdanghaetseumnida.
dialogue.en: For three years, starting two years ago.
What result did it produce?

dialogue.t: 응답 시간을 절반으로 줄였고, 만족도가 올라갔습니다.
dialogue.r: eungdap sigan-eul jeolban-euro juryeotgo, manjokdo-ga ollagatseumnida.
dialogue.en: I cut the response time by half and satisfaction rose.

lessons.title: 자기소개를 써요
lessons.learn: A self-introduction names a strength and proves it in one line: 강점은 문제를 끝까지 확인한다는 점입니다. A weakness is stated with what you do about it.

grammar.title: Naming a strength
grammar.pattern: 강점은 …라는 점입니다 · 성격이 꼼꼼한 편입니다 · 약점은 …라는 것입니다
grammar.explain: A strength is abstracted with -는 점이다: 강점은 끝까지 확인한다는 점입니다. The modifier form -는/은 makes a whole clause the subject, and 편이다 softens a self-description into a tendency.

examples.en: My strength is that I check a problem to the end.
I am on the careful side.

examples.t: 약점은 말이 느린 것입니다. 그래서 미리 준비합니다.
examples.r: yakjeom-eun mal-i neurin geos-imnida. geuraeseo miri junbihamnida.
examples.en: My weakness is that I speak slowly, so I prepare in advance.

mistakes.why: A strength is named as a clause with -는 점이다, not as an adjective.

mistakes.right: 약점은 말이 느린 것이고, 준비로 보완합니다.
mistakes.why: A weakness needs a remedy; 없습니다 answers the wrong question.

dialogue.en: What do you consider your strength?
My strength is that I check a problem to the end.
And your weakness?

dialogue.t: 말이 느린 편입니다. 그래서 중요한 자리에서는 미리 준비합니다.
dialogue.r: mal-i neurin pyeon-imnida. geuraeseo jungyohan jari-eseoneun miri junbihamnida.
dialogue.en: I speak on the slow side, so I prepare in advance for important occasions.

lessons.title: 지원 동기를 말해요
lessons.learn: Motivation connects the company's need to your own: 귀사의 …을 위해 일하고 싶습니다. The purpose form is -기 위해서, and the sentence ends in a wish rather than a demand.

grammar.title: Stating a motivation
grammar.pattern: 고객을 돕기 위해서 지원했습니다 · 여기서 성장하고 싶습니다
grammar.explain: Purpose takes -기 위해서 before the clause that realises it, and the clause ends in the verb that carries the intention: 지원했습니다 states it as the reason for applying.

examples.en: I applied in order to help customers.
I want to grow in this field.

examples.t: 제 경험이 팀에 기여할 수 있다고 생각합니다.
examples.r: je gyeongheom-i tim-e giyeohal su itdago saenggak-hamnida.
examples.en: I think my experience can contribute to the team.

mistakes.why: One intention, one predicate.
위해서 takes 을/를 on what the effort serves.

dialogue.en: Why did you apply to our company?

dialogue.t: 고객 문제를 해결하는 일을 계속하기 위해서 지원했습니다.

dialogue.en: I applied in order to keep solving customer problems.

grammar.title: Experience questions

lessons.title: 실적을 근거로 말해요
lessons.learn: An answer becomes convincing when it carries a number and a change: 문의가 삼십 퍼센트 줄었습니다. The result clause takes -ㄴ 결과, and what came about takes -게 되다.

grammar.title: Making a result concrete
grammar.pattern: 문의가 삼십 퍼센트 줄었습니다 · 개선한 결과 대기 시간이 짧아졌습니다 · 맡게 되었습니다
grammar.explain: Number plus change verb is the whole proof: 삼십 퍼센트 줄었습니다. -ㄴ 결과 links an action to its consequence, and -게 되다 states what you came to do without claiming you chose it.

mistakes.why: The figure carries the proof and belongs before the verb.

lessons.learn: Not knowing is answered honestly and then bounded: 잘 모르지만, 확인해 보겠습니다. The frame -지는 않지만 concedes before it adds.

grammar.title: Answering what you do not know
grammar.pattern: 잘 모르지만 확인해 보겠습니다 · 경험이 많지는 않지만 배우고 있습니다
grammar.explain: -지만 concedes and continues. -지는 않지만 limits the claim to one aspect while keeping the sentence open, which is how a first-year candidate answers without overclaiming.

examples.en: I do not know well, but I will check.
I do not have much experience, but I am learning.

mistakes.why: Not knowing is answered with the next step, not with a second negative.
-지만 needs a real continuation after the concession.

lessons.learn: Salary is discussed in ranges and with a question form: 희망 연봉이 어떻게 되세요? The answer states a range and leaves 협의 open.

grammar.title: Talking about pay

lessons.learn: The start date is a negotiation too: 다음 달 중순부터 가능합니다. To allow something, the form is -(으)ㄹ 수 있도록, and a change of plan is 통보하다.

grammar.title: Setting a date

lessons.title: 결과를 기다려요
lessons.learn: Waiting is phrased with a hope and a thank-you: 결과를 기다리겠습니다. 좋은 소식이 있었으면 좋겠습니다. A follow-up enquiry is 문의드리다, the humble form.

grammar.title: Waiting and following up
grammar.pattern: 결과를 기다리겠습니다 · 좋은 소식이 있었으면 좋겠습니다 · 문의드려도 될까요?
grammar.explain: A hope for the future takes -았/었으면 좋겠다, and the polite enquiry is the humble 문의드리다 with -(아/어)도 될까요? — asking permission rather than asking a question outright.

examples.en: I will wait for the result.
I hope there is good news.
May I enquire next week?

mistakes.why: A hope takes -았/었으면 좋겠다, not the plain condition.
One request frame; the humble form already carries the politeness.

culture.text: Korean hiring still carries the shape of the old 공채, the mass open recruitment, alongside 수시 hiring for individual posts. A CV is expected to be one page with numbers rather than adjectives, and 면접 usually runs as a panel with a fixed set of questions asked in a fixed order. Age, military service and graduation year once appeared on every form; today they are increasingly left off, and asking about them is treated as improper. What has not changed is the expectation that a candidate states a range and remains flexible: 협의 가능합니다.

reading.text: 지난달에 세 곳에 지원했습니다. 두 곳에서는 서류로 떨어졌고, 한 곳에서 면접을 보았습니다. 면접에서는 먼저 경력을 설명했습니다. 그다음에 가장 어려웠던 점을 물었습니다. 저는 일정 관리가 어려웠다고 말하고, 역할을 나누어 해결한 방법을 설명했습니다. 마지막으로 희망 연봉을 물었습니다. 저는 범위를 말하고 협의가 가능하다고 답했습니다. 결과는 다음 주에 통보받기로 했습니다.
reading.gloss: Last month I applied to three places. Two rejected me on paper, and I had one interview. In the interview I first explained my experience. Then they asked the hardest part. I said scheduling had been hard and explained how dividing the roles solved it. Finally they asked about salary. I gave a range and said it was negotiable. I am to be notified of the result next week.

task.title: Write a one-page CV and a ten-line interview
task.instructions: Draft four CV lines in 합니다체, each with a duty, a period and one number. Then write a ten-line interview: introduction, two questions with evidence-based answers, one question you answer with 잘 모르지만, and the salary exchange in which you give a range and say 협의 가능합니다.
